article.title: Cabinet clears a demand incentive of Rs 10,000 per kWh for electric two-wheelers, caps it at 15% of ex-factory price
article.text: The Cabinet approved a two-year demand incentive of ten thousand rupees per kilowatt hour for electric two-wheelers, capped at fifteen per cent of the ex-factory price and restricted to models meeting a fifty per cent domestic value addition threshold. The scheme replaces a lapsed programme under which the effective subsidy had fallen to about half this level. Ola Electric and TVS Motor Company both sell qualifying models today. Bajaj Auto, whose volumes are overwhelmingly internal combustion and whose electric portfolio is one model, is affected in the opposite direction only to the extent that the incentive shifts share within the commuter segment. The size of that shift is not estimated anywhere in the notification.
article.note: Substitution stories invite an 'ICE loser' claim that is a relative, unquantified statement. Relative disadvantage without a magnitude is uncertain -- displayable as a deep dive, never as a lead.

fact_items.text: Two-year incentive of Rs 10,000 per kWh for electric two-wheelers, capped at fifteen per cent of ex-factory price.
Requires fifty per cent domestic value addition; replaces a lapsed programme at about half the effective level.
No estimate of any share shift within the commuter segment is given in the notification.

quantities: ten thousand rupees per kilowatt hour

shocks.label: EV relative advantage
shocks.mechanism: A demand incentive lowers the effective retail price of qualifying electric models against unchanged internal-combustion prices, improving the relative total cost of ownership without changing anyone's absolute cost base

companies.name: Ola Electric Mobility
companies.mechanism: The entire portfolio qualifies and the incentive roughly doubles the effective per-vehicle subsidy against the lapsed scheme, cutting the on-road price of a pure-play maker's only product line
companies.rationale: Pure-play electric two-wheeler maker whose full range meets the value-addition threshold
positive_channels: effective retail price reduction on qualifying models

companies.name: TVS Motor Company
companies.mechanism: The qualifying electric scooter range gets the same effective price cut while the internal-combustion range is unaffected, so the incentive lands on the growing part of the mix
companies.rationale: Sells qualifying models today alongside an unaffected combustion range
positive_channels: effective retail price reduction on the qualifying range

companies.name: Bajaj Auto
companies.mechanism: A relative price shift toward qualifying electric models could move share within the commuter segment, but the notification estimates no shift and the combustion portfolio's own economics are unchanged
companies.rationale: Relative disadvantage of unstated magnitude with no change to its own cost or price
offsetting_channels: no change to the combustion portfolio's own cost or pricing

ground_truth.rationale: The two makers whose products actually qualify get a measurable price cut -- primary. The combustion incumbent's exposure is a RELATIVE claim of unstated size: uncertain is the honest verdict, and an uncertain verdict can inform a deep dive but must never lead the feed (INV-012). Publishing it as a confident negative would be inventing a magnitude the notification does not contain.
